text:
sara_support: Hey team, MoonRiver is hitting repeated 429s on their dedicated cluster during short bursts (spiky chat traffic). They report token-per-second SLO violations despite having burst credits. Can someone triage?

raj_oncall: Looking. Quick question — is this the cluster with 8xA40 reserved GPUs (mr-ded-08)?

sara_support: Yes. Customer claim: bursts ~3k TPS sustained for ~2m. Their console shows burst credits didn't decrease during the first 90s, then dropped to 0 and admission started rejecting.

mike_infra: Oof. I pulled admission-controller logs for mr-ded-08. Saw this around the window: `WARN admission: account=moonriver allowed_headroom=2400 used_headroom=2500 burst_credits=120 -> accounting_mismatch` then later `ERROR admission: debit_failed: insufficient_credits but cache says >0`.

alexa_prodeng: Can you paste the PromQL you used? I want to correlate with proxy and kernel metrics (latency/KV cache).

mike_infra: PromQLs I ran: `sum by(account) (rate(tokens_requested[1m]))`, `sum by(account) (rate(admission_allowed[1m]))`, and `sum by(account) (admission_burst_credits_total - admission_burst_credits_used)`. For moonriver during 03:12-03:16 UTC: requested ~2850tps, allowed ~2700tps, credits delta dropped from 115 -> 0 in 30s.

raj_oncall: Sounds like a race where allowed path didn't decrement credits immediately. Also seeing another tenant (orion-pay) consuming a lot of prefix cache which increased effective throughput. Could be noisy neighbor causing admission to mis-evaluate headroom.

sara_support: Customer included a trace showing 429s start after the third minute. They also showed billing page shows no extra burst authorizations.

mike_infra: Found an entry in the admission audit log that looks wrong: `{"ts":1976541999,"acct":"moonriver","op":"allow","credits_before":115,"credits_after":115}` — the `credits_after` never decreased for a few allow ops. Suspect ledger writeback failing when request path used routing fallback to local pool.

alexa_prodeng: Could be the retry path using a different admission client that doesn't call `debit_async`. We had a PR that introduced client pooling for low-latency fallbacks last month. @mike_infra can you grep for `debit_async` usage?

mike_infra: Grepped. Two places: one in `admission/main.go` and one in `admission/fallback_client.go`. The fallback has `// best-effort debit` comment and swallows errors. I can repro locally by simulating a transient write error to ledger: requests are allowed but credits not updated.

raj_oncall: Repro steps from my side: 1) start admission with `LEDGER_FAILPOINT=1` 2) fire 3k TPS for 90s from loadgen 3) observe credits don't decrement then suddenly drop to 0 when a sync job reconciles -> 429 flood.

sara_support: Customer impact: sustained SLO misses during that 90s window, some requests 5xx/429. They're asking for immediate mitigation and a short-term workaround (they want no more 429s).

mike_infra: Short-term mitigation options: a) patch fallback client to perform synchronous debit on allow (fast patch), b) apply per-account hard cap via route override: `max_tps: 3500` for moonriver so admission won't let neighbors steal effective headroom, c) restart admission-reconciler to force ledger sync (temporary). I recommend (a) + (c) for fastest.

alexa_prodeng: Agree. (a) is low-risk and should be rolled to canary. We'll also schedule a thorough postmortem and add a regression test: ledger write-back failure simulation.

raj_oncall: I'll open an incident ticket and run emergency patch canary. Steps I'm taking now: 1) apply emergency config bump to `max_tps` on mr-ded-08 for moonriver 2) deploy quick patch to fallback_client to stop swallowing errors 3) trigger reconciler restart.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered: `canary/admission-fallback-debit-sync` -> started 2/3 canaries.

sara_support: I informed the customer and offered temporary `max_tps` override and credits compensation if they want. They're okay with the temp override for now.

mike_infra: After canary looks good, we'll release to prod and add the ledger-failure unit test. Also adding an alert: `admission_credit_mismatch_ratio > 0.01` to catch when audit shows mismatches.

alexa_prodeng: Action items: mike - patch + tests, raj - incident + rollback playbook, sara - customer comms & credits estimate. ETA for patch roll: ~45m.

sara_support: thanks all. I'll update the ticket and ping MoonRiver when the canary completes. :thumbsup:
